intro: Carbohydrates fuel training, daily movement, and brain work. They also influence hunger, gym performance, and day-to-day scale weight through glycogen and water — which is why carb fear creates so much confusion.
buddyTip: Place most carbs around the meals and workouts where you need energy — and keep fibre-rich sources as the default.
mission: Choose one carb source you enjoy (oats, potatoes, rice, fruit, bread you actually like) and portion it on purpose at one meal.
why: Carbs are not villains. In a calorie-controlled, protein-adequate pattern, carb amount is a tool for performance and preference. Demonising them often leads to rebound eating of the exact foods you banned.
Higher-carb days can raise scale weight via glycogen and water even when fat is unchanged. Knowing that protects you from panic after pasta night.
Carb quality still matters for satiety and health patterns: fibre-containing carbs usually help more than sugar-sweetened drinks for the same energy.

points: Match carb intake to activity: harder training days often deserve more fuel
Prefer potatoes, oats, whole grains, fruit, and legumes when they fit your culture and taste
Liquid sugar is easy to over-drink and under-log
Low-carb can work for some; it is not mandatory for fat loss
Evening carbs are not automatically stored as fat — totals and weekly balance matter more

misconceptions.myth: Eating carbs after 6pm prevents fat loss.
misconceptions.truth: Timing myths distract from energy balance, protein, and sleep. Choose a schedule you can keep.

misconceptions.myth: Fruit is sugar, so skip it.
misconceptions.truth: Fruit brings fibre and micronutrients. Portions matter; fear is unnecessary for most people.

how.lead: Build a personal carb map for the week.
steps: List your training days and assign slightly higher carb meals there
Keep a default carb side you can cook half-asleep
Log sauces and sweet drinks that hitchhike with “simple meals”
If weight jumps after a high-carb day, wait for the weekly trend before changing everything
If energy crashes on low carb, add a measured portion back and reassess
how.buddyHelps: Foodiary captures carb-containing foods so Progress can show patterns across training weeks. Buddy coaching should protect fuel for hard days, not praise under-eating.

sections.title: Performance
paras: Hard sessions without carbs feel heroic once and stupid by week three. Fuel the work you ask your body to do.
If fat loss is the goal, create the deficit from the week’s average — not by starving every workout.

sections.title: Cultural foods
paras: Bread, rice, potatoes, and pasta are not moral categories. They are foods to portion inside your budget and fibre goals.
Sustainable plans keep cultural staples; they do not replace your cuisine with someone else’s grocery list.

mistakes.quote: I cut all carbs and wondered why lifts collapsed.
mistakes.why: Performance fuel dropped. Restore carbs around training and keep protein high.

mistakes.quote: The scale was up 1.5kg after a rice day so I panicked.
mistakes.why: Glycogen/water explains much of that. Watch the week.

mistakes.quote: I only eat “clean carbs” then binge on sweets.
mistakes.why: Rigid purity rules increase binge risk. Include planned enjoyable carbs.

encouragement: Carbs are a dial, not a demon. Turn them to fit training and hunger — then let weekly Progress tell you if the dial is right.
